rows.nowState: Implementation is COMPLETE. Acceptance is REJECTED and the reject STILL STANDS — but the ground under it is now clean and singular, which it was not an hour ago. SETTLED AT 21:59Z (D-129). The question D-128 raised and deliberately refused to answer in-house — the enumerated C1 fail clauses and the criterion's own title disagreeing — has been adjudicated independently by su-0300ecfc (eligible: no item implemented, no part of the rubric authored, outside the author's lineage, had not graded rev 9). Verdict: C1 = PARTIAL, CONFIRMING the author's own rating rather than overruling it. The reasoning generalizes: the enumerated clauses are a FAIL FLOOR, never a PASS CEILING — they say what forces a fail, never what earns a pass; the title governs pass, and the space between is exactly partial. A criterion is not passed by failing to fail. The deployment-position fallback is an alternative INSTRUMENT for determining liveness, not an alternative VERDICT that liveness holds. So the reject now rests on ONE ground and only one: the population-denominator remedy is committed on staging and ABSENT from the deployed sha 6e898b6cf8, re-measured 21:56Z and unchanged since at least 21:00Z. Adopted: any rubric edit would invalidate the standing attestation and both banked independent cards, and the author would be the beneficiary of the change. Filed as tracked work instead, to be taken only when a revision is already being paid for.

Owner killed a fleet by closing its terminals; the killed members' work-item leases (work_items.taken_by) were NOT released — persisted for the 6-day lease TTL, poisoning items for any successor. Owner directive (verbatim): "shouldn't our system have automatically unclaimed it as soon as I killed them... it shouldn't have to unclaim on a poll, it should be able to be done on a trigger when I close the console by listening to some event... We want a check to happen on a schedule too in case the event isn't fired for some reason, but it's better to get notified as soon as the console/session terminates." Root cause (grounded): (1) the presence reaper detects a dead session on a ~10-min idle poll but does NOT cascade to release that owner's leases; (2) the SessionEnd/Stop hook already FIRES on every psu session (hooks/cc/lifecycle-report.sh) but only posts a cosmetic activity marker; (3) work_items:release WITHOUT force:true returns ok:true while NOT clearing taken_by (should be not_holder); WITH force:true it DOES clear taken_by (verified on WI-4070). Release mechanism already exists — nothing invokes it on death, and non-force lies about success. See EI-9807 + EI-9808.

(2) Recomputing rerank scores externally cannot settle ordering — bucketing is round(score20), so a 0.9026 lands in bucket 18 while 19 needs >=0.925, and any small text-reconstruction difference flips the bucket. I nearly filed a false "rerank is discarded" defect on exactly that before catching it.

rows.nowState: FIX LANDED + GREEN. Root cause was an INVERTED TIMEOUT HIERARCHY, not a hang: measured opus at 62.4 tok/s => a full 4096-tok ideator response is ~66s vs a 180s cap (2.7x headroom), so the ideator CANNOT time out by generating. It was blocked in governor.acquire() waiting out a shared rate-limit pause (live depths 15s/120s/453s) and guillotined by an outer timer, then misreported as transport death ($0 spent, 0 ideas). One constant conflated time-to-GENERATE with time-waiting-for-CAPACITY. FIXED by separating the ADMISSION budget from the GENERATION budget: generation timer starts on admission (new onAdmitted seam), admission bounded by the cycle deadline (propagated scheduler->runner->cycle->ideators; the cycle recordingLlm wrapper bounds EVERY in-cycle call so no port can forget). All additive: no deadline => byte-identical old behavior. Guards: ideators 29/29 (5 new, incl. one that pins THE BUG: an admission wait longer than the generation cap must still succeed). tsc clean on all touched files. Also greened a live tsc red in scheduler.ts (reason union missing "no-capacity"). CORROBORATED by f69a7 WI-4541/4542 (gateway serialized the whole fleet through ONE admission slot; tiers ~inert) — that is WHY admission waits got long enough to blow the axe; their fix cuts the magnitude, mine stops the misreport + the cycle-eating.

rows.summary: Phase 1 (Arrow as the wire format) is independently valuable and carries no cache risk. Measured on a 6.65MB payload in V8: JSON.stringify+base64+TextDecoder+ JSON.parse = 55.1ms; a zero-copy format = 4.6ms (a bare memcpy). Arrow removes ~40ms of parse with no second source of truth and nothing that can go stale. Phase 2 (the…

rows.nowState: CLOSED ON ITS OWN GATE — negative result, recorded in full. P-001 ran the spike against real payloads pulled live from :3070 and Arrow LOST: net +20.9ms (server encode JSON 11.5ms vs Arrow 41.3ms; client decode JSON 11.5ms vs Arrow 2.5ms). Arrow is 4.6x faster to decode and 19% smaller on the wire, but tableFromJSON encode costs 3.6x JSON.stringify and swamps it. The earlier 55.1ms estimate that motivated this plan was wrong twice: it used a SYNTHETIC 12k-row uniform payload (V8's JSON.parse does our real ones in 3-9ms), and our rows are not tabular — 92% of plans.items is one nested item dict per row, 98% of plans.attention is a nested items list, so Arrow cannot infer them and they degrade to JSON strings inside Arrow columns. All remaining items dropped; see D-003 for the full data and for what would have to change before anyone re-proposes Arrow. Phase 2 (mmap cache) is moot — it existed to serve Arrow buffers.
rows.nowNext: Nothing here. Two follow-ups carry the value forward: WI-5910 (the REAL finding — plans.items/attention/list ship giant nested blobs; 65% of a 5.94MB wave, same three queries that are also the slowest resolvers; chokepoint is callPlansReadRaw per the 2026-07-19 audit) and WI-5911 (kill the base64 IPC leg, ~12ms, format-independent so unaffected by this gate). WI-5910 first — it is worth roughly 40x WI-5911.

rows.nowState: draft (v3). Supersedes papercusp-dogfood-v2-2026-05-22 after a vision refinement: collaboration is treated as the core experience, not a sync layer over a single-user model. Concretely: - Each contributor gets a long-lived user/ git branch + a worktree of that branch as their working directory. Branches are GitHub-pushed; the branch is the unit of in-progress work isolation. - Features stay in PG (HYPERBEE-synced); not on branches. v2 had me about to put feature files on user branches — that was wrong. Features are PG-canonical, Hyperbee-synced rows. The branch carries code only. - Queue and working state are Hyperbee rows pointing at features. Pulling a feature into your queue is a pointer, not a copy. - The orchestrator picks features no one else is working on (orchestrator-claim arbitrated by Hypercore sequence, no central lock). - GitHub is required for shared harnesses (PR + permissions surface). Behind a PrHost abstraction so GitLab/Gitea drop in later; v1 implements GitHub only. - PR lifecycle: agent ships code on your branch → PR opens to main → auto-approved if PR author's pubkey is on a pr-review role-holder's trust list, else manual review → merge flips the feature's status to shipped. - Trust is deliberate. No "trust anyone" toggle. A pr-review role-holder maintains their own trust list (LOCAL, never synced). - Sync-with-main is a UI gesture (status indicator + button + auto-rebase-on-push). One worktree per harness — main is a virtual view. Next action: review-and-revise this draft, then split into per-phase execution plans.
